questions.question_text:
A collection contains $430$ buttons.
How many buttons are $10\%$ of the collection?

options.why: Subtracted $10$ from $430$ instead of dividing the quantity by $10$.
Divided by $100$, finding $1\%$ instead of $10\%$.
Used the percentage number as the answer without applying it to the collection.

questions.question_text:
A recipe uses $520$ grams of oats.
What mass is $25\%$ of the oats?

options.why: Halved the mass once, finding $50\%$ instead of halving again for $25\%$.
Divided by $10$, finding $10\%$ rather than $25\%$.
Subtracted $25$ from $520$ instead of finding one quarter of the mass.

questions.question_text:
A length of cord is $34$ metres.
What length is $50\%$ of the cord?

options.why: Doubled the length instead of halving it to find $50\%$.
Divided by $10$, finding $10\%$ rather than $50\%$.
Halved the digits separately, discarded the fractional part of $3\div2=1.5$ to use $1$, then used $4\div2=2$ as the second digit.

questions.question_text:
A recipe uses $96$ grams of flour.
What mass is $25\%$ of the flour?

options.why: Divided $96$ by $2$, finding $50\%$ instead of $25\%$.
Multiplied $96$ by $4$ instead of dividing by $4$.
Read $25\%$ as one half and then multiplied $96$ by $2$ instead of dividing.

questions.question_text:
A ribbon is $7.8$ metres long.
What length is $50\%$ of the ribbon?

options.why: Divided by $10$, finding $10\%$ of the length rather than $50\%$.
Doubled the ribbon length instead of halving it.
Took $3$ wholes when halving $7$ wholes but discarded the remaining whole, then halved the $8$ tenths to get $4$ tenths.

questions.question_text: Find the difference between $25\%$ and $50\%$ of $260$ shells.

options.why: Added the two amounts, $65+130=195$, instead of finding their difference.
Reported $50\%$ of $260$ without subtracting the $25\%$ amount.
Used the $25$ percentage-point gap as the shell count instead of applying it to $260$ shells.

questions.question_text:
From an $80$ metre roll, $50\%$ is used for one project and $25\%$ for another.
How much remains?

options.why: Added the used lengths and reported the amount used instead of the amount remaining.
Subtracted only the $50\%$ section and ignored the additional $25\%$ section.
Treated $50\%$ and $25\%$ as $50$ metres and $25$ metres, then subtracted $75$ from $80$.
